answer: Use reef stewardship as the identity test. The registry gives an applicant one reef patch and a tray of coral kernels, each kernel dipped in a distinct pigment batch logged by spectrometer. The holder grafts kernels singly, filing a pigment-density photo after each graft; that reading unlocks the next permit. Divers reject pigment mismatches monthly. One identity takes 40 grafts, $520, and six months of visits; 1,000 identities demand 1,000 patches, $520,000, and 40,000 grafts, because a pigment batch authenticates only its own kernels and bulk orders create no second registered patch.
